items.entity: L-bracket arm widths (size of the removed corner)
items.description: Sec. 4 'Example designs' and the Fig. 4 caption only call this a 'classic L-shaped bracket' from the out-of-distribution set. Those problems come from parameterized problem classes with randomly drawn parameters (Sec. 3.1 Dataset, Sec. 3.2 Benchmarking problem sets). The widths of the vertical and horizontal arms, and so the size of the void corner, are never given. The text also does not say whether the two arms have equal widths.
readings: arm width a = 0.4L for both arms (0.6L x 0.6L void corner, classic L-bracket)
a = 0.2L (0.8L x 0.8L void corner)
a = 0.3L (0.7L x 0.7L void corner)
a = 0.5L (0.5L x 0.5L void corner)

items.entity: which corner of the square is cut away
items.description: Which corner is removed can only be seen in Fig. 4. The text gives only 'L-shaped', 'clamped support along the top edge' and 'downward point load applied at the right edge'. Together with 'classic', this suggests a top-right cut-out, but the text never says so.
readings: void corner at top-right: vertical arm on the left (clamped at its top), horizontal arm along the bottom (loaded at its right tip), the classic layout
void corner at top-left: vertical arm on the right, horizontal arm along the bottom
void corner at bottom-right (Γ-shape): horizontal arm along the top, vertical arm on the left

items.entity: how the cut-out is represented in the structured grid
items.description: Sec. 3.1 Dataset says material is kept out of part of the square domain by a mask ('for an L-shaped beam, the mask would be applied in the corner'). For the Fig. 4 problem it does not say how the mask is applied: whether masked elements are fixed void at E_min, whether they take part in the 2-pixel cone filter, or whether they are removed from the mesh.
readings: passive void elements (rho = 0, E = E_min) inside the full square grid, excluded from the filter
passive void elements inside the full square grid, included in the filter neighbourhood and reset to void after filtering
cut-out elements removed from the mesh (a true L-shaped mesh)

items.entity: prescribed volume fraction of the Fig. 4 instance
items.description: No volume fraction is given for this L-bracket. The out-of-distribution instances use randomly drawn parameters (Sec. 3.1/3.2). The only range given, U[0.12, 0.5], applies to the training set.

items.entity: reference region for the volume fraction
items.description: Eq. (2) in Sec. 3.2 prescribes the volume 'over the design domain Ω'. With a masked corner, it is unclear whether V0 is measured against the active L-shaped region or the whole square.
readings: V0 is a fraction of the active L-shaped region only (masked corner excluded)
V0 is a fraction of the full L x L square (masked corner counted as void)

items.entity: downward point load on the right edge
items.description: The Fig. 4 caption says only 'a downward point load applied at the right edge'. The height of the load on the tip of the horizontal arm is not given. Out-of-distribution instance parameters are random (Sec. 3.1), so the classic position cannot simply be assumed. Coordinates below have the origin at the bottom-left corner, with a = arm width.
readings: at the upper corner of the lower arm's tip: x = L, y = a (e.g. 0.4L)
at mid-height of the lower arm's tip: x = L, y = 0.5a (e.g. 0.2L)
at the bottom-right corner: x = L, y = 0

items.description: The load magnitude is not given anywhere for the compliance problems (Sec. 3.1, 3.2, 4).
readings: F = 1 (unit load)
any other magnitude (only scales compliance)

items.entity: clamped support on the top edge
items.description: The Fig. 4 caption says 'clamped support along the top edge'. This could mean only the top of the vertical arm, where there is material, or the whole top boundary of the square grid, including nodes above the void corner. If the corner is strictly void, the two give the same result; if not, they differ. Coordinates have the origin at the bottom-left corner, with a = arm width.
readings: clamp the nodes on y = L for x in [0, a] only (top of the vertical arm, e.g. [0, 0.4L])
clamp all nodes on y = L for x in [0, L] (the whole top edge of the square)

items.description: The FE mesh for the compliance benchmarks is never stated explicitly. Sec. 3.1 gives 64x64 grayscale designs, a cone filter radius of '2 pixels' and an 88-line-code set-up, which implies one element per pixel on a square domain. However, in the fracture example the decoder output is resized to a different mesh, so mesh = image grid is not certain.
readings: 64 x 64 unit-size square Q4 elements on a square domain, one element per image pixel
a finer grid (e.g. 128 x 128) with the design resampled to 64 x 64 images

items.description: Sec. 3.1 and Sec. 3.2 give only E0 = 1.0, Emin = 1e-9 and ν = 0.3, 'following the approach of the 88-line code'. The penalization exponent, which is a user input in that code, is never stated.
readings: p = 3 reached by continuation from p = 1

items.entity: 2-D elasticity assumption, thickness and element type
items.description: Plane stress vs plane strain, thickness and element type are not stated. They are only implied by 'set up following the approach of the 88-line code' (Sec. 3.1).
readings: plane stress, unit thickness, bilinear Q4 elements (as in the 88-line code)
plane strain

items.entity: MMA ground-truth optimizer settings and initial design
items.description: Sec. 3.1 says only that MMA was run 'with the default hyperparameter settings' for 200 iterations. It does not say which implementation's defaults (move limit, asymptote parameters) were used, or what the starting design was for the compliance problems. A uniform start is stated only for the fracture example.
readings: uniform initial density equal to V0, standard MMA defaults (e.g. move limit 0.5), fixed 200 iterations
uniform initial density equal to V0, MMA with move limit 0.2 (top88-style), 200 iterations
uniform start with a library MMA (e.g. NLopt LD_MMA) and its own defaults, 200 iterations

items.entity: volume-constraint form and its order relative to the cone filter
items.description: In Sec. 3.2, Eq. (2) enforces the volume by a sigmoid/bisection map, and the cone filter is 'the same set-up as for the MMA baselines'. The text does not say whether the volume is imposed on filtered or unfiltered densities, or whether the MMA baseline uses an equality or an inequality constraint.
readings: volume equality enforced on unfiltered densities by the sigmoid/bisection map, with the cone filter applied afterwards (Eq. 2 style)
volume inequality (<= V0) on the filtered physical densities (88-line style)

items.entity: thresholding used for the binary designs and compliances in Fig. 4
items.description: Sec. 3.2 'Performance metrics' says only 'the simplest strategy from [66]' for thresholding, and that strategy is not described. Only the heat-conduction section says densities are rounded to 0/1 'while preserving the volume fraction'.
readings: volume-preserving threshold: set the V0·N highest-density elements to 1 and the rest to 0
fixed cut-off at 0.5

locator: Sec. 4 'Example designs', Fig. 4 (the first problem instance shown with a design)
